Implement step A5 of the SFCC-83/84 Recently Viewed build plan (`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md`, section "### A5 — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` organism + recipe", lines 410-487). Branch: `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` (already checked out — do not switch branches).

## Files to create
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.stories.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.test.tsx`

## Files to modify
- `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — register the new `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` recipe (follow the existing registration pattern for other `ui-kits` organisms in this file).
- `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` — add `export const RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS = 5;` (named constant, with a short comment that it matches the Desktop Figma composition — see Cap below). Check this file's existing export style/grouping convention before adding.

## Explicitly do NOT touch
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts` — the new variation only needs `showBadge`/`showHoverImageSwap`, both already consumed in `zimmProductCard/index.tsx` from A2. If you find yourself needing to touch that recipe file, stop and report back rather than proceeding — it means something is modelled wrong.

## Component contract

Purely presentational — data arrives as props, no data-fetching:
```ts
type ZimmRecentlyViewedRailProps = {
  title: ReactNode;
  cards: readonly ZimmProductCardProps[];
  seeAllHref?: string;
  seeAllLabel?: string;
};
```
No `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` inside this component — the container (A6) owns any copy/intl. (The test file still needs an `IntlProvider` wrapper because `ZimmProductCard` itself calls `useIntl` — follow the exact wrapper pattern already used in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`.)

## Structure

Mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, "See Full History" link right, only rendered when `seeAllHref` is present) above a horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard` components, each rendered with `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` (the variation A2 already added).

**No rail-level arrow buttons** — `ZimmProductCard` already has its own intra-card carousel arrows; rail-level arrows would collide with them. Use native horizontal scroll with CSS scroll-snap only, nothing else.

## Responsive geometry — three explicit media queries, real Figma values (read 2026-09-06)

Import `breakpoints` from `app/theme/foundation` and write three **explicit `@media (min-width: ...)` blocks** — do NOT use Chakra's responsive-array shorthand (`['201px', '256px', '288px']` etc.); that shorthand fails this repo's `recipeGuards.test.ts` bare-token/structural guard. Follow the exact explicit-media-query pattern already used in `footer.css.ts` / `theme/components/footerShared.ts`'s `BP` constant, if you need a shared breakpoint reference.

| Viewport | Card width | Cards visible across |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile (base, no query — 402px design width) | 201px | 2 (201×2 = 402, full-bleed) |
| Tablet (`breakpoints.md`, 768px design width) | 256px | 3 |
| Desktop (`breakpoints.xl`, 1440px design width) | 288px | 5 |

All cards are a 2:3 aspect ratio — matches `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s existing `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` — so only card *width* varies per breakpoint; height follows from the aspect ratio, don't hardcode a height.

Header (`title-and-link` row) height: **96px on Desktop**, **56px on Mobile** — express as a token/var per the token rules below, not a raw px. The See-Full-History link is present at every breakpoint (never conditionally hidden by viewport — only conditionally hidden by the cap logic below).

## Token discipline (hard requirement — this is what `npm run audit:tokens` and `recipeGuards.test.ts` check)

- **Zero raw hex/px/rem/em literals.** Every value is either a `textStyle` (for anything textual), a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property (colour/spacing), or a named constant carrying an explicit `provisional`/`pending` comment if a genuinely new Figma value has no existing foundation token yet.
- **Zero bare Chakra/theme token strings** (e.g. `color="text.default"` or `gap="m"`) — always the `var(--zimm-*)` form instead. See `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` hierarchy points 1-2 and `.claude/rules/css.md` if you need the reasoning.
- **Recipe key must be namespaced `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`** — an unnamespaced key (e.g. just `RecentlyViewedRail`) will deep-merge with any same-named SFCC base recipe, which is wrong. Follow the `Zimm*`-prefix pattern already used by `ZimmProductCard`, `ZimmFooter*`, etc.
- **Declared `parts` must cover every part your component actually reads off `useMultiStyleConfig`** — `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` asserts this; under- or over-declaring parts fails it.
- **Zero `:focus-within` anywhere in the new recipe.** If you add any hover-reveal behaviour at all, its trigger must be `:hover, :has(:focus-visible)` — `:focus-within` stays matched after a click until focus leaves the subtree entirely, which has already caused a real stuck-open regression in this codebase (see `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s "Fix H"/"Fix J" comments for the actual incident if you want the detail). This rail likely doesn't need any hover-reveal at all (the link and cards are always visible) — only worry about this if you find yourself adding one.

## Cap — client-side only

At most `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (5) cards are rendered, regardless of how many are passed in `cards`. This must be a slice using the named constant, never a hardcoded `5` literal, and never something assumed to already be true of the input (the caller's API does not itself limit results, so the cap must be enforced here).

## Order preservation

Render `cards` in the exact order received (most-recent-first, left to right per AC 2) — no sorting, no reordering. Your own test for this must use a fixture where a *correct* rendering and an *incorrect* (e.g. reversed) rendering are visibly different in the assertion — don't write a test that would pass either way (e.g. asserting only "all 5 IDs are present" without checking their order/position). Prove this by literally reversing the fixture and confirming your own test fails, then revert — this is a fail-first requirement, not optional.

## Empty state

Render `null` when `cards` is empty (a second guard behind A4's visibility gate, which lives in the container, not here).

## See-Full-History link — exact token table (resolved from registered tokens, 2026-09-06 — do not re-derive)

| State | Treatment | Token |
|---|---|---|
| default | `textStyle="linkLg"` (already encodes `textTransform: uppercase` + `textDecoration: underline` — matches the Figma node exactly, don't add either property separately) | `typography.ts:152` |
| default colour | — | `var(--zimm-color-link-default)` |
| hover | colour shift only, underline persists (already part of `linkLg`) | `var(--zimm-color-link-hover)` |
| focus-visible | visible outline | `outline: var(--zimm-focus-ring)`, `outlineOffset: var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` (both from `zimmTokens.ts:68-69`) |
| active | no distinct token exists — inherit the hover colour, **with an inline comment saying explicitly that this is intentional inheritance, not an oversight** | — |
| disabled | not applicable — the link is simply absent (not rendered) below the cap threshold, never rendered-but-disabled | — |

**Add this exact caveat as a code comment near the link's styling:** no Figma hover/focus/active variant was found for this link (only `State=default` exists in the supplied nodes); the hover colour is *derived* from `colors.link.hover` — the only link-hover colour that exists anywhere in the design system — not read directly off a node. State this plainly so a future reader doesn't think it's a missed variant.

The See-Full-History link should only render when `seeAllHref` is provided AND (per B3, which wires the actual trigger condition later) — for A5 specifically, just render the link whenever `seeAllHref` is truthy; don't try to reimplement B3's ">5 cards" trigger logic here, that's the container's job in a later step.

## Storybook

- Story title: `'Commerce/ZimmRecentlyViewedRail'` (per `.claude/rules/components.md` categorisation table — Commerce-specific shared component).
- Named exports required: `Default` (5 cards), `WithSeeAllLink`, `SingleCard`, `OverCap` (pass 8 cards in, assert only 5 render).
- Add a `play` function on `WithSeeAllLink` asserting the See-Full-History link is keyboard-reachable (e.g. via Tab) and has the correct accessible name — follow this repo's existing `play` conventions (`.claude/rules/testing.md` Layer 2, query via `within(canvasElement)`, `getByRole` first choice).

## Vitest (`index.test.tsx`)

Test **only this component's own contract** — cap enforcement, order preservation (fail-first per above), empty-input renders `null`, link shown only when `seeAllHref` is present. Do **not** re-test `ZimmProductCard`'s own internals (badge rendering, hover-swap, accessible name concatenation, etc.) — that's already covered in `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx` per this repo's testing conventions (no duplicate coverage across layers). Wrap renders needing `ZimmProductCard` in the same `IntlProvider` pattern `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx` already uses.

## Before you report done

Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and fix anything you introduced. Do not run the full test suite or `audit:tokens` yourself — report back once the files are written and `tsc` is clean, and I'll run the fuller verification pass myself.

Report back: the exact files created/modified, a short summary of any judgment calls you had to make that weren't fully spelled out above, and confirmation `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan

**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out**; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met.
**No consent gating** (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-06) — must be stated in both PR
bodies; must not reach production.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.

**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.

Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
|---|---|---|
| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on `sessionStorage`. Failure degrades to `false`
  (no rail), never an exception.
- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
- Vitest: no flag + guest → `false`; flag + guest → `true`; no flag + registered → `true`;
  `sessionStorage` throwing → `false`; first render before effect → `false`.
- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct.
- The PDP change is exactly two lines. Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md
  Hard Rule #5 — no refactoring upward).

### A5 — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` organism + recipe

Create `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` (`index.tsx`,
`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`); register
`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

**Purely presentational — data as props.** Props: `title: ReactNode`, `cards: readonly
ZimmProductCardProps[]`, `seeAllHref?: string`, `seeAllLabel?: string`. No `useEinstein`, no
`useIntl` — the container owns the copy. (An `IntlProvider` wrapper is still needed in the test
because `ZimmProductCard` itself calls `useIntl`; follow `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`'s wrapper.)

Structure mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, See-Full-History link right) above a
horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s at `variation: 'recentlyViewed'`.

**No rail-level arrow buttons.** Desktop `40000307:12444` decomposes into exactly two children —
`title-and-link` (1440×96) and `group` (1440×432) — with no arrow layer. `ZimmProductCard` already
carries its own intra-card arrows; rail arrows would collide. Native scroll with scroll-snap only.

**Three explicit media queries** off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation`, never Chakra's
array shorthand (it fails `recipeGuards.test.ts`). Real geometry, read from the nodes 2026-09-06:

| Viewport | Rail node | Card | Cards across |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile (base, 402) | `40000538:25030` — 402×355.82 | **201×299.82** | **2** (201×2 = 402, exactly full-bleed) |
| Tablet (`breakpoints.md`, 768) | `40000730:13363` — 768×437.85 | **256×381.85** | **3** |
| Desktop (`breakpoints.xl`) | `40000307:12444` — 1440×528 | **288×432** | **5** |

All three cards are 2:3, matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s existing `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` — so card
width is the only thing that varies per breakpoint; height follows. Header (`title-and-link`) is
**h96** on Desktop (`40000538:20306`) and **h56** on Mobile (`40000538:25031`); the link is present on
both, so it is never hidden by viewport.

**Pass criteria**
- **Every value is `textStyle`, `var(--zimm-*)`, or a named constant with a `provisional`/`pending`
  comment.** Zero raw hex/px/rem/em, zero bare Chakra token strings. `npm run audit:tokens` reports no
  new finding here; `recipeGuards.test.ts` passes (namespacing + bare-token guards).
- Recipe key namespaced `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` — an unnamespaced key deep-merges with any same-named
  SFCC base recipe.
- `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` passes — declared `parts` cover every part read off
  `useMultiStyleConfig`.
- **Cap is client-side.** At most `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (5, matching the Desktop
  composition) regardless of input length. Finding 29: the API ignores `limit`, so the cap cannot live
  in the request. Named constant, never a literal.
- **Order preserved verbatim** — renders `cards` in received order, most-recent-first, left to right
  (AC 2). Test with an input whose correct and incorrect orderings are distinguishable (**not** a list
  already order-independent — that is exactly the encoded-bug trap). Make it fail by reversing.
- Renders `null` when `cards` is empty — a second guard behind A4's gate.
- **See-Full-History link states — RESOLVED FROM REGISTERED TOKENS 2026-09-06, not from the
  `zimmNavItem` fallback (which is now known to be wrong for this link).** The Figma default state
  (`40000138:469`, *"State=default, Size=Large"*) is `Default/Link-lg`, uppercase, **underlined at
  rest**, colour `--alias/color/link/default` `#191919`. The old plan borrowed `zimmNavItem`'s
  "underline appears on hover" — impossible on a link that is already underlined.

  Every piece is already registered in this repo's Tier 1 foundation, so nothing is invented:

  | State | Treatment | Token |
  |---|---|---|
  | default | `textStyle="linkLg"` — **already encodes `textTransform: uppercase` + `textDecoration: underline`**, so it matches the node exactly | `typography.ts:152` |
  | | colour | `var(--zimm-color-link-default)` (= `grey[900]`, matches `#191919`) |
  | hover | colour shift only — underline persists | `var(--zimm-color-link-hover)` (= `grey[500]`) |
  | focus-visible | `outline: var(--zimm-focus-ring)`, `outlineOffset: var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` | `zimmTokens.ts:68-69` |
  | active | no distinct token exists — inherit hover, with a comment saying so | — |
  | disabled | N/A — the link is absent below the threshold, never disabled | — |

  **Honest caveat to carry in a code comment:** no Figma hover/focus/active *variant* was located
  (the symbol name implies a `State` axis, but only `State=default` exists in the supplied nodes and
  `search_design_system` finds no "Link" component set). `colors.link.hover` exists in the
  designer-owned foundation for exactly one purpose and is the only link-hover colour in the system,
  so deriving hover from it is defensible — but it is a derivation, not a node reading.
- **If any hover-reveal is added, its trigger is `:hover, :has(:focus-visible)` — never
  `:focus-within`**, which stays matched after a click until focus leaves the subtree entirely and has
  already caused a stuck-open regression here (`zimmProductCard.css.ts` Fix H/J).
- Story titled `Commerce/ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (`components.md` > Categorisation). Named exports
  `Default` (5 cards), `WithSeeAllLink`, `SingleCard`, `OverCap` (8 in, 5 rendered). A `play` on
  `WithSeeAllLink` asserting the link is keyboard-reachable with the right accessible name.
- `index.test.tsx` asserts this component's own contract only — cap, order, empty-null,
  link-shown-when-href-present. Do not re-prove `ZimmProductCard`'s internals (`testing.md`).

### A6 — Wire the container branch; remove the copy-first markers

In `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`: add one branch. When
`recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, map `recommendations.recs` through A3's
mapper and render `<ZimmRecentlyViewedRail>` gated by A4's `hasRecentlyViewed`; otherwise render
`<ProductScroller>` exactly as the faithful port does. Remove A1's `console.log`.

Import `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` by **relative path** — `overrideStyling.md` > "Importing an
already-overridden component" exists because `.storybook/main.js` and `vitest.config.ts` do not load
the overrides resolver.

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	import { CARD_SLOT, HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY, DESKTOP_QUERY } from '../../zimmProductCardShared';

4	/**
5	 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
6	 * arrows/indicator split — now a shared import from `zimmProductCardShared.ts` rather than each
7	 * file's own module-private copy, so the two can't silently drift. Governs the price <->
8	 * size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage together off the
9	 * exact same media feature, on this shared root.
10	 */
11	
12	/**
13	 * A viewport-width gate, unrelated to `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above — governs the PLP-only bag-icon
14	 * mobile hide (Fix D, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) below. Also a shared import from
15	 * `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, same reasoning as `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` above: this and
16	 * `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`'s own `root` padding step both need the identical `min-width`
17	 * gate, and a module-private copy in each file was exactly the drift risk this extraction removes.
18	 */

20	type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
21	  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
22	   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
23	  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
24	  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
25	   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
26	  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
27	  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
28	   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
29	   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
30	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
31	  /** Fix C — true whenever ZimmProductCardContent actually mounted a notify-me button
32	   *  (`isUnavailable && onNotifyMe`, computed once in index.tsx as `showNotifyMe`). Unlike the two
33	   *  flags above, the "hidden by default" half lives INSIDE `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`, not outside it
34	   *  — see docblock point 4: a touch pointer must see notify-me unconditionally (confirmed via
35	   *  every Mobile Unavailable Figma reference), where price/the size-selector do the opposite. */
36	  hoverRevealsNotifyMe?: boolean;
37	  /** Fix C — true for a PLP/Wishlist card that would normally hover-swap to the size-selector
38	   *  (`config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector`) but is out of stock. Unlike every other flag here, this
39	   *  is not a pointer-type concern at all: the size-chip wrapper stays hidden permanently, in
40	   *  every state, on every device — see docblock point 4. */
41	  sizeSelectorUnavailable?: boolean;
42	  /** Fix D — PLP only (`VARIATION_CONFIG.plp.hideBagOnMobile` in index.tsx). A viewport-width
43	   *  concern, not a pointer-type one: hidden below `breakpoints.md`, visible from it up — see
44	   *  docblock point 5. */
45	  hideBagOnMobile?: boolean;

48	/**
49	 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
50	 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
51	 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
52	 * own by itself:
53	 *
54	 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
55	 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
56	 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
57	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
58	 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
59	 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
60	 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
61	 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
62	 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
63	 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
64	 *      Four separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
65	 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
66	 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
67	 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but four plain keys need no such
68	 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
69	 *      ONE of the four (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
70	 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
71	 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close`, `carousel`, and `media` are the three
72	 *      exceptions: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly
73	 *      (`close` via `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute,
74	 *      top: 50%, ...`; `media` — its own root — via `position: relative`), so each needs (and
75	 *      gets) only the z-index bump here:
76	 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
77	 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
78	 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
79	 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
80	 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
81	 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
82	 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
83	 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
84	 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
85	 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
86	 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
87	 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
88	 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
89	 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
90	 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
91	 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
92	 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
93	 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
94	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
95	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
96	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
97	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
98	 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
99	 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
100	 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
101	 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
102	 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
103	 *        - `media` — Fix I (SFCC-236, found via a real mobile-device touch-swipe check performed
104	 *          after this branch's own live testing round, not by any automated pass). The media/
105	 *          gallery scroll region itself was never added to this lift list, even though it is
106	 *          exactly as interactive as the controls nested inside it: with no z-index of its own,
107	 *          `[data-card-slot="media"]` sat at the same default/auto stacking layer the overlay
108	 *          itself occupies, so a touch swipe starting on the image landed on the invisible
109	 *          overlay `<a>` first and the real scroll container underneath never received the
110	 *          gesture — the slide indicator still rendered correctly (proving the image data/gallery
111	 *          logic was fine), but nothing paged. Missed earlier because `close`/`carousel`/content-
112	 *          buttons were each checked with a real CLICK (Fix 1, Fix 3 above) — and a click on the
113	 *          image happened to "work" by accident either way, since it also landed on the overlay
114	 *          `<a>` and still navigated to the PDP — so nothing about a plain tap ever surfaced this;
115	 *          only a real SWIPE (which needs the scroll container itself, not the overlay, to be the
116	 *          hit target) exposed the gap. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position:
117	 *          relative` (its own recipe), so, same as `close`/`carousel`, only the z-index bump is
118	 *          needed here — plus `cursor: 'pointer'`, since this element is no longer inside the
119	 *          `<a>` that used to convey that affordance via the browser's default link cursor. Fixing
120	 *          this the same way used to fix `close`/`carousel` necessarily breaks the accidental
121	 *          click-still-navigates behaviour described above (media no longer lets the click reach
122	 *          the overlay at all) — restored deliberately via a real `onClick` on
123	 *          `ZimmProductCardMedia` instead of relying on the overlay by accident: see index.tsx's
124	 *          own docblock for the click-passthrough narrative, and its `handleMediaClick`, which
125	 *          guards the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real `<button>`
126	 *          descendants of `media`) so they keep doing only their own thing.
127	 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
128	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
129	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
130	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:has(:focus-visible)` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below,
131	 *      superseded by Fix H — see point 6) — `:hover` alone would leave every reveal permanently
132	 *      unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable device.
133	 *
134	 *      Fix J (SFCC-236, this fix — full defect + fix write-up lives at the end of point 6):
135	 *      "hidden" and "revealed" are expressed via `position`/`clipPath`, not `display`, at every
136	 *      site in this block. `display: 'none'` used to mean "hidden" here, but `display: none`
137	 *      unconditionally strips an element from the accessibility tree, not just from paint — see
138	 *      point 6's own Fix J note for the full defect this caused. Hidden is now `position:
139	 *      'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` (out of flow, paints nothing — identical visual/layout
140	 *      footprint to `display: none` — but stays in the DOM, tab order, and accessibility tree);
141	 *      revealed is `position: 'static', clipPath: 'none'` (back in normal flow, painted again) —
142	 *      the exact technique `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` already ships for its own off-page

144	 *      byte-for-byte unchanged by Fix J — only the property values inside these blocks changed.
145	 *   4. NOTIFY-ME'S HOVER GATE (Fix C, found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit against the
146	 *      real Figma Default+Hover Unavailable instances for all three variations, desktop AND
147	 *      mobile). Three behaviours confirmed together, all different from point 3 above:
148	 *        - `isUnavailable` suppresses the PLP/Wishlist size-selector swap entirely (index.tsx
149	 *          AND-s `hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` with `!isUnavailable` before they
150	 *          ever reach this recipe) — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price
151	 *          stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own `hoverRevealsPrice` is
152	 *          untouched by this — its Unavailable Hover reference still reveals price normally.
153	 *        - Suppressing that swap is not, by itself, enough to reproduce the reference: with no

155	 *          (visible) default and would show permanently — briefly shipped exactly that way mid-fix
156	 *          and caught by re-checking the real render against Figma, which shows size chips hidden
157	 *          in BOTH states when unavailable, not merely "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
158	 *          (index.tsx: `config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && isUnavailable`) carries that permanent
159	 *          hide as its own unconditional rule below — deliberately outside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`
160	 *          entirely, since unlike everything else here this isn't a pointer-type distinction at
161	 *          all: every device sees it hidden, full stop.
162	 *        - Notify-me itself is hover-gated the OPPOSITE way round from price/the size-selector:
163	 *          hidden by default and revealed on hover **only inside `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`**, not
164	 *          unconditionally. Every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it appearing only on
165	 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
166	 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no
167	 *          reveal needed. Putting the "hidden by default" half outside the media query — matching
168	 *          point 3's own structure literally — would have made notify-me permanently invisible on
169	 *          touch, since a touch pointer never matches `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` and so could never
170	 *          trigger the `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` half either.
171	 *   5. THE BAG ICON'S PLP-ONLY MOBILE HIDE (Fix D, same SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit). A genuinely
172	 *      different axis from points 3-4 above: `DESKTOP_QUERY` is a **viewport-width** media query
173	 *      (`min-width`), not `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`'s pointer-capability one — a large touch tablet and
174	 *      a small hover-capable laptop window need to agree with Figma's own Desktop/Mobile split by
175	 *      width, not by input method. Figma's PLP/PDP Mobile Card-content instance
176	 *      (`40002163:41479`) has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`; Desktop's own PLP
177	 *      instance and Wishlist's Mobile instance (`40002187:58472`) both leave it visible — so this

180	 *      `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable`, Fix G's narrower Wishlist-only-when-out-of-stock rule —

564	        // the same `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` shape as the price/size-selector swap above.
565	        // Fix J: `display: 'flex'` stays here (unlike the other four sites' reveal rules, which
566	        // drop `display` entirely) — `clipPath: 'none'` is ADDED alongside it, not instead of it.
567	        // See docblock point 6's own Fix J note for why: this part needs `display: flex` for its
568	        // own `justifyContent`/`alignItems` layout, and nothing else asserts that once
569	        // `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s own unconditional `display: 'none'` is replaced by
570	        // `clipPath`. `position` is deliberately absent from both entries below, also unlike the
571	        // other four sites: this part is `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally already (Media's
572	        // own vertical-centring rule), and toggling it to `'static'` here would break that
573	        // centring the instant the arrows are revealed.
574	        //
575	        // Fix K (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a hover-capable
576	        // pointer needs its OWN not-yet-revealed base state here — `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s
577	        // own `carousel` part reverted to an unconditional `display: 'none'` (Fix K there), which a
578	        // hover-capable pointer must override to `flex`/clipped before `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`
579	        // below can reveal it at all; without this, the arrows never render even on desktop. Touch
580	        // pointers never enter this media query, so they correctly keep the unconditional
581	        // `display: 'none'` and never become tab stops for a control they can never reveal.
582	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
583	          display: 'flex',
584	          clipPath: 'inset(50%)',
585	        },
586	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
587	          display: 'flex',
588	          clipPath: 'none',
589	        },
590	        // Fix J belt-and-braces (see docblock point 6 and the new lift-adjacent rule in point 2
591	        // above): re-enables the arrow buttons' hit-testing only once genuinely revealed.
592	        [`&:hover [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
593	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
594	        },
595	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"]`]: {
596	          display: 'flex',
597	          clipPath: 'none',
598	        },
599	        [`&:has(:focus-visible) [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.carousel}"] button`]: {
600	          pointerEvents: 'auto',
601	        },
602	      },
603	
604	      // 5. PLP-only bag-icon mobile hide — see docblock point 5. A separate, sibling media-query
605	      // key from HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY above (a viewport-width gate, not a pointer-capability one).
606	      // Mobile-first: hidden by default, shown again from the shared [DESKTOP_QUERY] block below.
607	      ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
608	        [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'none' },
609	      }),
610	
611	      // Fix F+D's shared desktop-reveal block — deliberately ONE `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key,
612	      // not two. A first version of this recipe gave `sizeSelectorUnavailable` and
613	      // `hideBagOnMobile` each their OWN separate `...(condition && { [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {...} })`
614	      // spread (mirroring how every other flag in this file gets its own independent spread) —
615	      // which silently broke, because both spreads produce a property with the exact same
616	      // *computed key string* (`'@media (min-width: 48em)'`) on the same `root` object. Object
617	      // spread is a SHALLOW merge: it does not deep-merge two spreads that happen to share a key,
618	      // it just lets whichever spread comes LAST overwrite the earlier one's value entirely. With
619	      // `hideBagOnMobile`'s spread positioned after `sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s in this file, its
620	      // `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object silently replaced the other's, and the price-reveal-on-desktop
621	      // rule vanished from the actual emitted CSS — confirmed for real via
622	      // `document.styleSheets` in a live browser (price stayed `display: none` at 1280px width
623	      // despite `window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48em)').matches` correctly reporting `true`);
624	      // every jsdom test still passed, because each one only ever sets ONE of the two colliding
625	      // flags at a time, never the realistic combination a genuine unavailable PLP card produces.
626	      // `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` above never had this problem because it was always written as a
627	      // single key with every contributing condition spread INSIDE it — this block now follows
628	      // that same shape.
629	      [DESKTOP_QUERY]: {
630	        ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
631	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.price}"]`]: { display: 'block' },
632	        }),
633	        ...(hideBagOnMobile && {
634	          // 'flex', not 'block': ZimmProductCardContent's own `bagWrapper` part sets
635	          // `display: 'flex'` (it centres the icon inside via alignItems/justifyContent) — this
636	          // organism's `[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="bag"]` selector has higher
637	          // specificity (a class + two attribute selectors vs. Content's own single class) and
638	          // would win the cascade either way, so restoring the actual display type Content uses
639	          // matters here, not just "anything visible" — 'block' would silently flatten that
640	          // wrapper's centering.
641	          [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.content}"] [data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.bag}"]`]: { display: 'flex' },
642	        }),
643	      },
644	    },
645	  }),
646	};
